messages:
GammaHealth Support: Hey team, between ~11:58–12:05 UTC we saw a spike of 429s from /v1/generate in us-east-1. No raised latency, just immediate 429s. Can you check whether this is a quota or server-side issue?

Sara K: Thanks — can you paste a minimal request example and one X-Request-ID from a 429 response?

GammaHealth Support: Sample payload attached (sanitized). One X-Request-ID: req_01GZ9X8Y. We saw ~120 RPM and ~900–1100 TPM in our logs but it's bursty — many requests within <10s windows.

Mike P: Are these coming from a single region / IP range or multiple clients? Any upstream proxy that might be multiplexing?

GammaHealth Support: Single region (us-east-1), a handful of app nodes behind an internal proxy. No obvious proxy re-use, but they do open short-lived connections during cron bursts.

Alex R: On Redwood side I see rate-limit events for that key during the window. Our per-key limits are applied with token-bucket refills: even if average RPM looks fine, short bursts can deplete tokens and cause 429s.

Julio (ops-bot): Alert: key=kh_live_XXXX hit rate limit at 2026-02-12T11:58:40Z -> 2026-02-12T12:06:05Z; peak RPM 138, peak TPM 1152.

Lisa H: Two quick checks: 1) confirm client concurrency/retry loop behavior, 2) capture response headers like `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset` from one 429 so we can see exact window alignment.

GammaHealth Support: We pulled one 429 response, headers below: `X-RateLimit-Limit: 100/1000`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-RateLimit-Reset: 23`. Looks like their token bucket is 100 RPM and 1000 TPM.

Sara K: That lines up. If your client sends many requests in a tight loop (eg 40 requests in 5s) you'll exhaust the bucket even if 10s later the RPM average is fine. Can you confirm request distribution?

GammaHealth Support: Our cron fans out to 6 nodes and each node issues 20 parallel requests during syncs. So short concentrated bursts for ~20–30s.

Mike P: Two mitigations: a) Smooth client side with small jitter + token backoff, b) increase quota for the key while you deploy smoothing. We can offer a temporary quota bump if needed.

Lisa H: Also check connection reuse/keepalive vs new TLS handshakes — too many new connections can look like spikey traffic. If using HTTP/2 multiplexing one upstream connection with many streams still counts as many requests but is easier to smooth.

Alex R: For repro, please run a controlled test from your infra so we match the pattern. Example test (on a single node):

```
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{url_effective} %{time_total}\n" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"xlarge","input":"hi"}' \
    https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate &
done
wait
```

Run that with and without sleeps (eg `sleep 0.2`) and with concurrency flags to see when 429s start. Send us the output of the first 20 lines that show 429s.

GammaHealth Support: We'll run that in a staging subnet and send logs. If we confirm burstiness, what's the fastest client change?

Sara K: Add a randomized jitter on cron task start times (spread 30–60s), limit per-node concurrency (eg cap to 4 inflight requests), and implement exponential backoff on 429 (start 300ms -> *1.5). That usually fixes immediate production pain.

Lisa H: As a temporary safety-net we can bump your key to 200 RPM / 2000 TPM for 24h while you roll out changes. I can action that if you confirm time window and commit to smoothing rollout.

GammaHealth Support: Please do the 24h bump for the next business day window, will run tests overnight and push smoothing config in the morning. Also attaching one full request/response pair and our app logs.

Julio (ops-bot): Change request logged: quota bump request #Q-9234 by Sara K -> 200/2000 for 24h starting 2026-02-13T08:00:00Z (pending approval).

Mike P: I'll approve the temporary bump once we get confirmation of test plan. Also adding a note: if traffic is coming from a small pool of IPs we can suggest routing policies or per-route limits to avoid cross-tenant impact.

Alex R: Follow-up item for engineering: consider exposing a per-key burst profile graph in Console (heatmap of short-window bursts) — would make troubleshooting these cases faster. Filing internal ticket.

Sara K: Thanks everyone. GammaHealth — once you run the curl repro, paste the first 10 lines showing 429 and one `X-RateLimit-*` header snapshot and we'll flip the quota bump. :thumbsup:

GammaHealth Support: Will do. Appreciate the quick help! :raised_hands:
